chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: “If a man and a woman are found in a single covering, and proof is established against them for that, and nothing beyond that is discovered from them, each one of them is to be flogged one hundred lashes.”

So this report may be understood to mean one whom the Imam had already rebuked, disciplined, and forbidden from that because of an act previously done by him, then later found him having returned to the like of his action; at that point it would be permissible for him to establish the hadd upon him in full. This interpretation is also supported by the earlier reports, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَدَّبَهُ: disciplined him with corrective punishment short of the full hadd
key_terms.إِقَامَةُ الْحَدِّ: carrying out the prescribed legal punishment in full
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam as the rightful authority implementing discipline and legal punishment
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةُ: legally established proof or evidentiary testimony
key_terms.جُلِدَ: was flogged as a corporal legal punishment
key_terms.لِحَافٍ وَاحِدٍ: a single covering or blanket shared by the man and woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a man and woman found together under one covering?
ai.summary: This report addresses a legal ruling concerning a man and a woman found together under one covering when legal proof is established. The appended discussion explains that the ruling may apply to one who had already been warned and disciplined by the Imam, then repeated the act, thus justifying the full hadd.
